versions.text: Verify that functional compatibility of the integrated system is safe. DoD/MIL Doc: JSSG-2001B: 3.3.1.1/4.3.1.1

Criterion: Verify that functional compatibility of the integrated system is safe. Standard: Engine/Air Vehicle interfaces maintain functional compatibility throughout all normal operating and flight conditions. Hazardous conditions to interfacing subsystems do not result from normal or abnormal operation of the associated subsystem. Critical functional interfaces are fault tolerant or fail safe to the extent that no single failure or combination of failures results in an unacceptable risk in accordance with 7.1.1. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, simulation, demonstration, inspection and review of documentation. Engine/Air Vehicle functional interface requirements are verified by inspection of program documentation such as interface control and design documents. Integrated system functional compatibility is verified by simulation, test and demonstration of system functionality at integration test facilities and on the air vehicle during ground and flight test. Engine/Air Vehicle functional hazards and probability of air vehicle loss are verified by inspection of System Safety documentation.

Standard: Engine to air vehicle interfaces maintain functional compatibility when operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1 for the stated life documented in engine technical data. The engine control system does not propagate any functional failures to the air vehicle. Failure(s) of the air vehicle and propulsion communication system results in a fail-safe capability that allows continued engine operation without exceeding engine operating limits. For multi-engine (three or more engines) air vehicles, an engine shutdown is permissible if the shutdown does not result in loss of air vehicle. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., interface control and design documents, hardware drawings, design data records, inspection reports, photographs, or other substantiating records and reports) to verify the functional capability of the engine to air vehicle interfaces. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is conducted to verify the functional capability of the engine to air vehicle interfaces. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Installed engine ground testing is conducted to verify integrated system functional compatibility of the engine to air vehicle interfaces. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (2) Flight test: Flight testing is conducted to verify integrated system functional compatibility of the engine to air vehicle interfaces.
